_note: Canonical tag vocabulary. Everything filters on these. Closed list — adding a tag means adding it here first, with a one-line description, or table validation fails at import.

space.indoor: enclosed by walls or a roof — filters gate and archetype pools that assume shelter
space.outdoor: open to the sky — the opposite pole to indoor
space.underground: below ground level — caves, cellars, tunnels; distinct from indoor for filtering and prose

light.lit: bright enough to see by without a carried light source
light.dim: poorly lit — sits between lit and dark for filtering and prose
light.dark: no ambient light — needs a carried light source to see or act safely in

traffic.path: a through-room with exactly two connections, neither branch nor destination
traffic.open: a wide, unconstrained space — a plaza or clearing, no single obvious route through
traffic.dead-end: exactly one connection — a branch's terminus, matched against a room type's max-degree fit
traffic.junction: three or more connections meet here — a hub of movement through the area

use.dwelling: someone lives here — a home, a den, a nest
use.storage: goods are kept here — cellars, larders, stockrooms
use.workspace: work happens here — a forge, a workshop, a kitchen
use.shrine: a place of worship or ritual, however small
use.market: goods change hands here — stalls, counters, a trading floor
use.ruin: broken down and abandoned — no longer used for its original purpose
use.grave: the dead are kept or buried here — a crypt, a barrow, a graveyard plot
use.cell: a small, confining room meant to hold someone — a prison cell, a cage

nature.wild: untamed by hand — undergrowth, rock, or wilderness pressing in
nature.cultivated: shaped and maintained by people — farmland, gardens, tended ground
nature.water: open water or its immediate edge — a stream, a well, standing water
nature.stone: built or carved from stone — masonry, rock walls, a cave chamber
nature.wood: built or grown from wood — timber construction, or a stand of trees
nature.flooded: standing water covers the floor — a wetter, more hazardous kin of water
nature.settled: civilised and maintained — the opposite pole to wild, marks a room as part of an inhabited place

mood.quiet: still and undisturbed — nothing pressing happens here
mood.grim: bleak and foreboding — the room reads as a bad sign
mood.lush: abundant or richly appointed — nature or wealth in excess
mood.austere: spare and unadorned — deliberately plain, nothing wasted
mood.corrupt: tainted — morally, magically, or physically fouled
mood.holy: sanctified — the room carries religious or sacred weight
mood.opulent: conspicuously wealthy — fine materials, excess on display

feature.landmark: a notable point of interest — narrows a hub-shaped area's centre-room roll (e.g. a town's market square)
feature.vantage: a high or open point with a view over the surroundings
feature.hazard: eligible for a placement roll of a dangerous-looking curio (a pit, a rotten floor) — flavour, not a stat effect
feature.concealment: cover to hide in or hide something — gates where stealthy creatures, secretive NPCs and investigate-quest objectives can be placed
feature.hearth: a fire or its equivalent — warmth, a gathering point, often a dwelling's centre
feature.safe: no gate to another area is ever placed here — a guaranteed-quiet room
feature.private: somebody's specific interior — a shop, a home, a cell; excluded from the entry-room roll so the player never lands inside someone's shop

taxonomy.beast: a natural animal — no higher reasoning, acts on instinct
taxonomy.humanoid: human-shaped and human-minded — people, in the broad sense
taxonomy.undead: dead but still moving — animated by something other than life
taxonomy.construct: built, not born — golems, animated armour, mechanisms
taxonomy.fey: otherworldly and capricious — not of the mortal order
taxonomy.demon: infernal in origin — malice given a body
taxonomy.plant: vegetal and rooted in nature rather than flesh

mind.mindless: no will of its own — acts on instinct or a single directive, never negotiates
mind.cunning: plans and adapts — the most dangerous kind of opponent to underestimate
mind.proud: will not back down easily — pride outweighs self-preservation
mind.maternal: protective of its own — young, nest, or kin change how it fights
mind.timid: quick to flee or avoid a fight it isn't sure of
mind.relentless: does not stop pressing once it starts — rarely breaks off
mind.kind: well-disposed by nature — more likely to talk than fight
mind.curious: drawn to investigate rather than attack outright
mind.venal: motivated by gain — can be bought off or bribed

build.armoured: naturally or physically well protected — harder to land a solid hit on
build.swift: fast — hard to pin down, quick to close or flee
build.hulking: large and powerful — hits hard, likely slow
build.frail: physically weak — goes down easily once hit

appetite.hungry: driven by literal hunger — food, or the player, is the target
appetite.lustful: driven by desire — shapes how it approaches and what a Presence check plays against
appetite.greedy: driven by wanting more — treasure and gain motivate it
appetite.vengeful: driven by a grudge — holds and acts on a wrong done to it

kind.weapon: used to fight with — the basis of a weapon-track attack
kind.shield: carried to block or deflect — a defensive off-hand item
kind.light: a light source — pushes back darkness in a dark room
kind.tool: used to interact with the world rather than to fight — a key-like utility item
kind.key: opens a specific lock or door
kind.consumable: used up on use — a potion, a ration, a one-shot item
kind.treasure: valuable for its own sake — no mechanical use beyond its price
kind.curio: an oddity — flavour and value, no mechanical function
kind.container: holds other things — a chest, a sack, a corpse's belongings
kind.door: blocks or grants passage — may be locked, may need a key

quality.crude: the lowest quality tier — cheap, rough, least effective
quality.plain: ordinary quality — no particular craft either way
quality.masterwork: the highest quality tier — exceptional craft, rare and valuable

trait.heavy: encumbers more than its size suggests
trait.fragile: breaks or degrades easily — handle or use with care
trait.cursed: carries a hidden cost — flavour, something about it works against its holder
trait.blessed: carries a hidden benefit — flavour, sanctified in the holder's favour
trait.stolen: not rightfully the holder's — flavour, carries a consequence if recognised
trait.sealed: closed and not meant to be opened without cause — a locked or warded container
trait.untradable: cannot be sold or traded away — enforced on the item's flags

operators.any: dark|wild       — must have at least one
